answer: An agent economy can prove each identity occupies a distinct physical location: several independent beacon nodes send a timed signal, and the agent must answer each within a narrow latency window. Like water seeping through karst, the signal travels a unique path to every real machine, so answers from a thousand fakes sharing one rack in a frozen tundra of servers arrive with identical timing and are merged into one identity. Buying real machines in real places for every fake costs more than the fraud earns, while one honest agent answers its own beacons cheaply.
